16.	On April 18, 1983, Joan Benoit won her second X Marathon in the women's division with a time of 2:22:43, shattering the previous record by nearly three minutes. The following year, she went on to win the first-ever women's Olympic marathon at the 1984 Summer Games in Los Angeles, solidifying her status as a legend of distance running. The X Marathon itself holds a unique distinction among the world's major marathons: first run in 1897, it is the oldest annual marathon in the world. The course runs from the town of Hopkinton in the suburbs to downtown X and is famous for a series of punishing hills between miles 16 and 21. The last and most infamous of these hills, near X College, acquired the legendary nickname Y after the 1936 race, when defending champion Johnny Kelley patted the shoulder of the leader, Ellison "Tarzan" Brown, on the uphill — only to see Brown surge away and break Kelley's spirit.
